ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The voltage waveform in the attached figure takes θ as the horizontal axis, marks one period from 0 to 2π, and has jumps at π/3, 2π/3, 4π/3, 5π/3, and 2π. The vertical axis marks +100 V and -100 V. Throughout the entire period, the horizontal segments of the waveform are only located at +100 V or -100 V, and the jump vertical lines are instantaneous changes and have no area contribution to the root-mean-square integral. Reasoning: Calculate RMS over one period from 0 to 2π. Since the voltage amplitude of the waveform in all effective time intervals is 100 V, that is, v(θ)=+100 V or -100 V, after squaring they are all v^2(θ)=100^2=10000. The average value of the squared value over one period is still 10000, therefore Vrms = sqrt(10000) = 100 V.

method.method_draft: Identify one full period on the θ-axis, 0 to 2π. From the graph, note that each segment of the waveform is either +100 V or -100 V. Square the waveform for the RMS calculation: both positive and negative segments become 100^2. Average this constant squared value over the full period and take the square root to get 100 V.
